verdict.line: You lose if you let Nasus free-farm into a stacked late game; you win if you deny his Siphoning Strike stacks before he hits level 6.

brief.thesis: Irelia holds lane and solo-kill advantage early because Nasus's entire power budget is tied to landing Siphoning Strike last-hits, and Irelia's dash-reset kit lets her zone him off minions. The 46.6% head-to-head win rate over 1222 games reflects what happens when that denial window is wasted — Nasus scales into a monster that outlasts short trades.

theirWindow.when: Level 6+, once Wither lands on you
theirWindow.what: Wither (15/14/13/12/11s cooldown) kills your movement and attack speed, which sets up Fury of the Sands (120s cooldown) draining your max health. Do not start or continue a fight once Wither is on you post-6.

yourWindow.what: Chain E (Flawless Duet) to stun and Mark him, then Q (Bladesurge) to dash in and refresh off the Mark. He has no mobility to escape this and no answer to the stun lock.

powerCurve.note: E stun punishes his short-range Q trades
Q resets off Marks let you all-in freely

start.why: The 47.7% win rate line over 1318 games — the extra sustain and damage lets you win the early all-in trades that deny his stacks.

boots.why: 48.3% win rate pick — reduces the physical damage from his autos and Siphoning Strike during the extended trades this lane demands.

core.why: Current-health damage and the slow proc let you land kills during your early-game all-in windows.
Follows the 54% win rate path over 174 games — lets you punish his need to stay on lane to farm stacks.
Completes the top-performing build line — the damage-over-time conversion offsets his Soul Eater sustain in extended fights.

situational.when: he's stacked Siphoning Strike heavily and fights are dragging into sustained skirmishes
you need more single-target burst to close out all-ins before his Wither lands

runes.keystoneWhy: The ramping adaptive force and healing reward the extended trades you're forcing, and directly offsets his Soul Eater sustain.

summoners.why: 85.3% pick rate — Ignite punishes your level 2-5 all-in windows and denies the healing Soul Eater would otherwise give him back.

playing.title: Deny every last hit you can
playing.detail: Nasus's entire scaling is tied to Siphoning Strike (8/7/6/5/4s cooldown) landing kills on minions. Use E's stun to zone him off farm whenever you have it up.

playing.title: All-in hard before level 6
playing.detail: Chain E's Mark into Q's dash-reset for repeated burst. He has no dash or hard CC to punish this before Fury of the Sands comes online.

playing.title: Track his Wither cooldown
playing.detail: Wither (15-11s cooldown) cripples your movement and attack speed. Don't commit to a long trade or chase while it's available.

playing.title: Stay out of Spirit Fire
playing.detail: Standing in the flame patch strips your armor over time, which snowballs his Siphoning Strike damage on top of it.

playing.title: Respect post-6 Fury of the Sands
playing.detail: The 120s-cooldown ultimate grants him bonus health, range, and max-health drain. Don't start fights on cooldown timers you haven't tracked.

playing.title: Cash out at max passive stacks
playing.detail: Wait for Ionian Fervor's bonus attack speed and on-hit damage to peak before committing to the kill, rather than forcing it on cooldown.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, and win rates are measured from live OP.GG games on the current patch; the lane-phase reasoning and cooldown tracking above are my own tactical read.

stats.opponentTip: Keep a strong hold over lane control since early game to prevent Nasus from easily growing. Do not get caught off guard and nuked when Nasus uses (R).
